title: Osaka Metro Tests AI Robot Station Worker
paragraphs: Osaka Metro, the company that runs the subway in Osaka, has tested a humanoid robot that works as a station attendant.

The robot is called "Hinata." It was made by the telecom company KDDI and a company called AVITA. The head of AVITA is Hiroshi Ishiguro, a professor at the University of Osaka and a famous robot expert. The robot uses Gemini, an AI model made by Google.
The test started on August 31, 2026, at Umeda Station, a very busy station in Osaka. In September, the robot was also tested at Tanimachi-kyuchome Station.

The robot answers questions from passengers. For example, it tells them how to change trains and where to find tourist spots near the station. It can speak about 60 languages, including Japanese, English and Chinese. It can also show a code that people can scan with their smartphones to get directions.
When one person asked the robot where to find good takoyaki, it recommended shops on a nearby food street. On the first day, it answered people's questions without any problems.
Passengers enjoyed meeting the robot. One man said it was new and interesting.

Why is Osaka Metro testing the robot? Like many companies in Japan, it is worried about not having enough workers. The company will use the results of the test to decide whether robots like this could help. A spokesperson said the company wants to see if humanoid robots can offer new value to customers.
Osaka Metro has tested robots before. In 2025, it tested a different robot that used AI at Umeda Station.
